transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-10-28
- Time: 09:00 PT / 12:00 ET
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Priya (CTO Verdane), Jordan (Lead ML Eng), Marta (Infra), Ben (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Verdane BI is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted + dedicated deployment. Primary concerns: p95 streaming latency (sub-300ms target on short dialogs), burst capacity for token storms (they see spiky traffic with ~6-10k concurrent chats during peak), deterministic failover when dedicated capacity fills (fallback to hosted), and proof that quantized model variants won't regress quality. They requested a pilot to run token/sec benchmarking and a failover simulation.

Topics discussed:
- Current infra and traffic profile
- p95 latency targets and token/sec goals
- Streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs
- Dedicated capacity + hosted fallback topology
- Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, VPC)
- Benchmarks and pilot plan

Action items (extracted): see metadata action_items field above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood, with Samir our lead SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya: good, thanks. we wanted to get into the nitty gritty today, especially around p95 streaming latency and what happens when we get a token storm.
[00:15] Samir: great, that's exactly our sweet spot. quick qual question — what does a typical session look like? avg tokens per session? and what's your p95 target?
[00:24] Jordan: so most sessions are short, 2-6 turns, avg token output maybe 80-120 tokens. but during promos we see long-running flows — up to 2k tokens — and bursts where concurrent sessions jump to roughly 6k. p95 goal is 250-300ms for streaming acknowledgements (we know full completion will be higher for long completions).
[00:41] Marta: also important — we have strict data residency for some customers, and anything PHI-ish needs to stay in our VPC. we're evaluating dedicated or private for that tier.
[00:50] Alex: makes sense. couple of clarifying points: when you say streaming p95 250-300ms, is that the first-byte latency for a stream chunk, or the time to first token?
[01:01] Priya: first chunk, yes — and for short prompts the full answer should be effectively real-time. for long prompts we can tolerate higher completion time but we care about tail behavior.
[01:10] Samir: ok. in Redwood we typically measure streaming p95 as time-to-first-chunk and also track per-token emission time. we can instrument token/sec and per-request kv cache reuse. note the KV cache is sometimes transcribed as K-V cache in our notes, you'll see that in logs, but it's the same thing.
[01:25] Ben: how deterministic is failover? if dedicated pool saturates do you splice to hosted and maintain session continuity? that's critical for UX.
[01:33] Samir: good question. our routing supports per-request policy. in practice we recommend a canary fallback: if dedicated can't accept new requests within X ms we route to hosted model variant we've pinned to the same model family and quantization profile. streaming continuity depends — you'll likely see a reconnect but we can stitch responses using client-side replay so UX is smooth. we can demo a failover simulation in the pilot.
[01:53] Jordan: what's the observed overhead when you do that? reconnects and re-priming the prompt could add lots of tokens and time.
[01:59] Alex: it's a tradeoff. we instrument to minimize re-priming — prefix caches and delta prompts. typical overhead we've seen in similar customers is 40-120ms extra to re-warm per session for short dialogs when fallback is immediate, but it's workload dependent. for long completions the overhead is comparatively small.
[02:18] Priya: also, cost — how much more for dedicated vs hosted? we need to present numbers to finance.
[02:24] Alex: we'll send a dedicated vs hosted worksheet — basic rule: dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower per-token CPU/GPU overhead for high sustained throughput; hosted is cheaper for infrequent spiky loads but less predictable p95 at scale. for your mix (sustained baseline ~800-1k concurrent with 6k spikes) we usually suggest a modest dedicated pool sized for baseline plus autoscale/burst into hosted for peaks.
[02:45] Marta: our infra team needs specifics about networking egress rules; we run strict SAML SSO with our IdP and need KMS integration for keys. can Redwood integrate with our HSM?
[02:56] Samir: yes — we support KMS integrations, HSM-style key wrapping for private deployments. for Hosted we have a managed encryption-at-rest offering and can show our SOC 2 docs. for Private deployments we can deploy within your VPC and integrate with your HSM, although on-prem air-gapped setups require additional planning.
[03:15] Jordan: on performance testing — what does your benchmark harness look like? we want to run token/sec tests and also streaming p95 tests with synthetic user distributions.
[03:24] Samir: we provide a harness (scripts + dockerized loadgen) that can replay your real request traces or synthetic distributions. we recommend three phases:
- Phase A: single-worker microbench (measure tokens/sec, GPU utilization, quantization variants)
- Phase B: steady-state multi-worker (replicate baseline concurrency, check tail latencies)
- Phase C: burst/fanout simulation (rapid ramp to target spike, exercise failover and routing)

[03:50] Priya: can we prescribe specific quantization? we care about int8 vs int4. quality drop is sensitive.
[03:56] Samir: absolutely. we'll test fp16 baseline, int8 quant, and int4 (where supported), and run an eval set you provide. we track quality delta metrics (perplexity is meh for our use case; we prefer task-based evals). we'll include recommended quant profile per model.
[04:12] Ben: how long would the pilot take? team is under timeline pressure — target is Q4 buyer decision.
[04:18] Alex: pilot can be 2 weeks for a minimal throughput + failover sim, with results and a follow-up review in week 3. we can compress to 10 working days if you provide traces and evaluate parallel resources.
[04:28] Priya: timeline's tight but doable. Jordan, can you surface the traffic traces?
[04:33] Jordan: yes, we can export sampling for the past 90 days. one note — our spike patterns are sporadic, not sustained; the last promo produced 22k rps for 90 seconds across their mobile clients.
[04:46] Marta: that 22k number is pretty scaring, we need both burst cap and graceful degradation. we prefer graceful degrade to errors.
[04:52] Samir: we have a couple strategies: pre-warmed burst pools, controlled shedding (lowest-priority requests), and adaptive batching to reduce per-token cost while maintaining throughput. also fail-open to hosted variant is an option.
[05:06] Alex: and from an SLA perspective we can set per-route SLOs. you asked about p95 at 250-300ms — realistic for short dialogs on a dedicated pool with proper batching and streaming enabled. for long-running completions p95 will be higher; we surface these metrics at token-level in console so you can separate first-chunk latency from full-completion latency.
[05:28] Jordan: how do you measure p95 for streaming? is it across all chunks or first chunk only?
[05:33] Samir: we provide both: p95 time-to-first-chunk, p95 per-chunk inter-arrival, and full-completion p95. the dashboard lets you slice by model, region, and route.
[05:43] Priya: security and audit — we need audit logs and request-level tracing for compliance. can you retain logs in our S3 for 12 months?
[05:51] Samir: yes for Dedicated and Private we can push audit logs into your S3 with customizable retention. Hosted has a managed retention, but enterprise packages can custom configure retention windows and export.
[06:03] Ben: what about cold-starts? we saw a vendor where single-request p95 spiked due to cold model loads.
[06:09] Alex: cold-starts are typically seen when an entire worker goes idle and then receives traffic. our dedicated pools keep a minimum resident capacity and we have warm-up policies; plus we can pre-warm models on demand before big promos. we'll include recommended min-resident parameters in the pilot spec.
[06:24] Jordan: can you run a controlled failover where some percent of requests are throttled and the rest routed to hosted, and show rebuilt session latencies? we want numbers not theory.
[06:34] Samir: yes that's exactly part of the burst/fanout Phase C. we'll instrument the reconnect overhead, re-priming token counts, and time-to-first-chunk after failover.
[06:46] Priya: do you support pinning model versions? we need determinism across rollout.
[06:50] Alex: yes, model pinning and rollout policies (canary, A/B, instant rollback) are supported. rollouts can be route-level.
[06:57] Marta: one subtlety — our infra uses HTTP/2 streaming and we need gRPC in some services. does Redwood support both?
[07:04] Samir: yes we expose both REST/HTTP streaming and gRPC streaming endpoints. we'll share sample clients.
[07:11] Ben: what's the expected tokens/sec on a single A100-like worker for your standard LLM we tend to use (7b-ish)?
[07:19] Samir: depends on quant and sequence length, rough numbers: fp16 7b ~ 1.2-1.8k tokens/sec per GPU in streaming mode with continuous batching; int8 can be ~1.6-2.4k under the right kernel choices. we'll validate on your workload.
[07:36] Jordan: how does batching affect p95? we don't want p95 to degrade because of batching waiting for a batch to fill.
[07:42] Samir: continuous batching only delays when it's beneficial; we configure latency budgets per route so if p95 target is strict we reduce batching and accept lower throughput. the Optimize tool suggests batching params to balance cost vs latency for your SLOs.
[07:56] Priya: regarding network egress and routing — if we pick dedicated in a cloud region, can we failover to hosted in a different region automatically?
[08:04] Alex: yes routing policies are region-aware. automatic fallback across regions is supported but increases latency; for critical customers we recommend multi-region dedicated pools to avoid cross-region fallbacks.
[08:16] Jordan: ok, last technical Q — how do you prevent KV cache stomping when many small sessions hit the same model keyspace? we saw cache thrash in our internal infra.
[08:25] Samir: we have per-client cache partitioning and eviction policies tuned for conversational workloads; we also do prefix caching and can pin embeddings to reduce re-computation. during the pilot we'll surface cache hit rates and tune accordingly.
[08:38] Priya: sounds good. let's talk costs briefly — if we size dedicated for baseline 1k concurrent, and then hosted for burst, what's the expected monthly delta vs fully hosted?
[08:48] Alex: rough back-of-envelope: fully hosted for your peak patterns will be expensive because of frequent bursts; a small dedicated pool (~4-6 GPUs depending on model choice) to serve baseline plus hosted burst will often be 25-40% cheaper month-over-month. we'll give a precise model after we see traces.
[09:05] Ben: can you also include failure-mode SLOs and runbook examples in the next doc? our ops team likes playbooks.
[09:12] Alex: yes, runbooks and suggested fallbacks included.
[09:16] Priya: great. for the pilot, our acceptance criteria: meet p95 <= 300ms first-chunk for short dialogs in 90% of test cases, demonstrate failover with reconnect overhead <= 150ms on average, and show quantization that keeps task-level quality delta < 2%.
[09:33] Samir: we'll aim for those in the test plan and flag any areas we think are unrealistic up front.
[09:40] Jordan: small nit — transcription in your notes spelled KV as 'kay vee' sometimes which confuses the docs, but it's fine.
[09:46] Alex: thanks for flagging.
[09:48] (overlap/crosstalk) Marta: okay, timeline — we need the bench plan this week to align finance.
[09:54] Alex: we'll get the benchmark + pricing worksheet by Tuesday (2026-11-02). Samir will attach the test harness and pilot steps.
[09:59] Priya: thanks everyone.
[10:02] Ben: thanks, talk soon.
